newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- eyes on data, budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- eyes on data, budget.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mostly flat in early Thursday trading, with attention centered on data releases and prospects for a budget accord.
"Most of the quotes are pretty much where they were last night and most of the deals have been placed," one trader said.

A second trader said one potential market mover Thursday is the 1000 EDT release of the National Association of Purchasing Management Index for April, which is expected to hit 53.6, compared to 55.0 for March.
The day's earlier figures were a "non-event," the trader said.

The U.S. Commerce Department said March personal income rose 0.6 percent, while spending increased 0.5 percent. Jobless claims rose to 347,000 the week of April 26 from a revised 319,000 the previous week, the Labor Department said.

Another focus Thursday will be news reports on the progress toward a budget accord. Muni prices gained ground Wednesday along with other fixed income markets, in part by reports that Congress and President Clinton were nearing agreement on a new budget.
With additional reports early Wednesday that an accord was in reach, the government long bond was up 6/32 at 96 to yield 6.94 percent.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2020 were four basis points lower at 5.93 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2025 were unchanged at 5.76 percent.
Debt futures were higher, with June municipal futures up 5/32 to 114-17/32 and June Treasury bonds 6/32 higher at 109-15/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 162 ticks from 163 at the close on Wednesday.

Supply this week has been modest, but preliminary figures show a large pick-up next week. Negotiated sales alone are expected to hit just over $3 billion, divided among 36 issues, according to the Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
